solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unable to resolve galaxy

indicators.note: to resolve something is to break it down and rework it, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An astronomer's telescope cannot make out a distant galaxy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to resolve' looks like telescope talk about bringing a fuzzy image into focus, but it signals the anagram of UNABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Before distant star systems were understood, galaxies were catalogued as spiral nebulae, so the old astronomical term covers one.

clue.text: All the same, exact fare only

definitions.meaning: nothing is different; everything stays as it was
a bus sign telling passengers that drivers give none back from cash handed over

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both that a situation is unaltered and that a driver hands back no coins.

clue.text: Book about way volunteers make garden's social hub

indicators.note: the book word goes about, wrapping around, the other letters

parts.note: the Bible is the Book
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A book about how volunteers can create a community garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve; 'Book' is the Bible by crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised feeding platform in a garden is where birds gather, a playful social gathering place.

clue.text: Old group dressed in green to be delayed

indicators.note: the old group is dressed in green, so those letters are placed inside the colour word

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A veteran band turns up in green costumes, running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in green' reads as costume, but it means placed inside a word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall behind schedule is to be held up and let minutes slip away, hence being delayed.

clue.text: Foolishness as 25 swim off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of place, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, the word meaning reverse or cancel

explanation.surface: Calling off a swim, or undoing one, seems a silly thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of the letters of the 25 across answer (UNDO) together with SWIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom is good judgement, so its negation, an old formal word, is a lack of sense or folly.

clue.text: New trial doesn't start getting close

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a hearing is a court trial

explanation.surface: A retrial that hasn't begun is fast approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearing means coming nearer to something, so approaching or drawing close to it.

clue.text: Bring in Chief Inspector's terrible writing

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so all these letters are jumbled

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for a Chief Inspector of police, plus S for the 's

explanation.surface: Bring in the police chief, whose handwriting is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles BRING IN with CIS (CI, Chief Inspector, plus S).
explanation.definitionFit: Inscribing is carving or writing letters onto a surface, so it is a form of writing.

clue.text: See about northern poet

indicators.note: the dating word goes about, surrounding, the northern letter

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to date them

explanation.surface: An instruction to look up a poet from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a cross-reference instruction, but it means go out with: DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval Florentine wrote the Divine Comedy, the great Italian poem of the afterlife.

clue.text: Notice central Exeter's shopping area

parts.note: to notice is to mark, as in mark my words

indicators.note: the central letters of the city name are taken

explanation.surface: A sign spotted in the middle of Exeter's shopping district.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter, a city in Devon, has six letters; its two central ones give ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A market is a place where stalls sell goods, a traditional shopping area in a town.

clue.text: Perhaps Leo and Al will send a message

parts.note: Leo is an example of a star sign of the zodiac
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two friends, Leo and Al, are going to send a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo and Al look like two men, but Leo is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: To signal is to communicate by gesture or a light, transmitting information without words.

clue.text: Woman is right outside breaking crockery

indicators.note: the inner letters break into the crockery word, splitting it apart

parts.note: china is fine porcelain crockery

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right sits outside the word is, wrapping it

explanation.surface: A woman stands to one side as plates and cups smash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' and 'breaking' nest one insertion inside another. The name links to 29 across: Christina Rossetti was the Victorian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so any woman bearing it fits; the definition is deliberately vague.

clue.text: Getting rid of the director is smoother and more reasonable

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so a letter comes out of the smoother word

parts.note: a sander is a tool that smooths wood
D is an abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A workshop is improved, and calmer, once the boss who wields the sander goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoother' reads as a comparative adjective but is a noun here: the sanding machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Saner is the comparative of sane, meaning of sounder mind and judgement, hence more sensible.

clue.text: Faculty splits when Pence disappears

indicators.note: when a letter disappears it is dropped from the word it was in

parts.note: to split something is to part it, so parts means splits
P is the abbreviation for pence in British money

explanation.surface: A university department divides when the money runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pence' looks like a person, perhaps a politician, but it is the British coin abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities group humanities subjects into a division called Arts, one faculty among several.

clue.text: Faint stirring with light wind eradicating black car chemical

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of faint are rearranged
eradicating removes completely, so a letter is taken out of the wind word

parts.note: a breeze is a light wind
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A faint breath of breeze stirs the chemical smell of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' gives ANTIF from FAINT, and 'eradicating black' takes B from BREEZE to leave REEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Antifreeze is the glycol mixture added to a car's radiator coolant to stop it icing in winter.

clue.text: Preserved cucumber offered — I'll pick Lebanese bottles

indicators.note: the phrase bottles, or holds inside it, the letters needed, running across word breaks

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper says they will choose Lebanese jars of pickles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' is a verb meaning contains: the letters run from offereD to LEbanese.
explanation.definitionFit: A gherkin or small cucumber preserved in brine with dill herb is this deli staple.

clue.text: Angel chewing a gerbil

indicators.note: chewing mangles food, so the letters of a gerbil are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A heavenly being is gnawing on a small pet rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewing' is the anagram signal; read it as what the gerbil does to its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is the archangel who announces the birth of Jesus in the Bible.

clue.text: Almost lose sight of evil sprite

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: to lose one's sight is to go blind

explanation.surface: A wicked fairy nearly makes someone go blind.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore this is a small, ugly, mischievous creature, a malevolent kind of sprite.

clue.text: Possibly 15 here not getting up after one cocktail

indicators.note: the reversed word comes after the first two pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a sling is a gin cocktail, as in the Singapore sling

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up reads the word from bottom to top

explanation.surface: An angel stays upright after one too many cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is GABRIEL, an Angel: Angel is a district and Tube station in this north London borough. 'getting up' reverses NOT to TON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angel is a well-known area at the heart of this London borough, so one Angel may be found there.

clue.text: Commercial magazines pulling out nearly all stops for a bit

parts.note: an ad is a commercial on television

indicators.note: the shortened word is pulled out of the magazines word

parts.note: journals are magazines or periodicals

indicators.note: nearly drops the final letter of all

explanation.surface: An advertising magazine almost stops publishing for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' is AL, and 'pulling out' removes it from JOURNALS to leave JOURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a meeting is to suspend it, breaking off temporarily until a later time.

clue.text: Bond's report came up

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: to bond metal parts is to weld them, and weld is the word heard

explanation.surface: James Bond's mission report surfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is the verb to join; spoken, WELD sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that wells rises to the surface, as tears or a spring does, so it came up.

clue.text: Cross about initially making advances to boss's poodle

indicators.note: about turns the cross word round, reading it backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix in a church

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: An angry person chases off an employer's pet poodle that made unwelcome advances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is ROOD, a church crucifix; 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle, figuratively, is a servile follower; someone people walk over is the same kind of submissive lackey.

clue.text: Made a complete mess of connecting light to plug

indicators.note: connecting joins the light to the plug, one placed straight after the other

parts.note: a bung is a stopper or plug
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light

explanation.surface: Someone botched the job of wiring a lamp to a plug.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is electrical, but the plug is a bung (a stopper) and the light an LED.
explanation.definitionFit: To bungle is to handle something clumsily and ruin it, so the past tense fits made a mess of.

clue.text: Grows British clarinets?

parts.note: clarinets are reed instruments, sometimes called reeds; the question mark flags this example

explanation.surface: A British orchestra's woodwind section grows.
explanation.walkthrough: Clarinets are played with a reed, so musicians call such instruments reeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed animals or plants is to raise them, so a farmer who breeds stock raises and grows them.

clue.text: Superb finish stopping clock beam

indicators.note: the letter stops up the clock word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a timer is a clock for timing

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A superb finish in a race halts the clock beam.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber means wood cut for building, and especially a single wooden joist or beam.

clue.text: Surprisingly dim person I locked up

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests something turning out unexpectedly, so these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A dim-witted individual was, to everyone's surprise, put in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' scrambles DIM PERSON to give MPRISONED, with the clue's final I placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprisoned means confined in a jail or cell, which is the sense of being kept behind bars.

clue.text: Entreaties mostly make someone happy

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to please someone is to make them happy

explanation.surface: Begging requests usually succeed in cheering people up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleas are earnest appeals or requests, the same sense as entreaties.

clue.text: Oddly missing turn, idiot has to reverse

indicators.note: dropping the odd-placed letters leaves only the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the words

explanation.surface: An idiot who misses the turning has to back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' looks like driving, but it is the definition: to undo is to reverse an action.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo an action is to cancel or reverse it, as with a computer's undo command.

clue.text: See 3
Cold and windswept lake Bill crosses

indicators.note: the bill word crosses over the lake letter, so it sits around it

parts.note: a bird's bill is its beak
L is an abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill walks across a chilly, exposed lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak describes exposed open country that is chilly and battered by wind, like moorland.

clue.text: In very cold conditions I'd win term after advancing money

indicators.note: advancing moves a letter forward, here from the end of the phrase to its front

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
M is an abbreviation for money, as in economics

explanation.surface: A student wins a term's grant in the depths of a frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after advancing money' says the final letter standing for money moves to the front of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Midwinter, the depth of winter around the solstice, is the season of the coldest weather.

clue.text: Some macros set time at 10 or 7:15

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A computer user sets up some macros to run at a fixed time.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'at 10 or' was wrong: 'at' is a link, and the definition is '10 or 7:15', the answers CHRISTINA or DANTE GABRIEL, both poets of this surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina and her brother Dante Gabriel were the Victorian poet siblings sharing this family name.

clue.text: One German paper includes small deceptive attacks

indicators.note: the paper word includes the German word, holding it within

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, the paper this puzzle appears in
ein is German for one
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A German newspaper runs small stories about sneaky attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Feints are mock blows in fencing or boxing, made to draw a defender off guard.
